questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the correct collocation. **

Motorists committing this infraction are _______ fined.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: heavily

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Collocation is the combination of words formed when two or more words are often used together in a way that sounds correct.
 
• Let us look at the meaning of the given words.
 
 
• Wholly: Entirely; fully. (पूर्णत)
 
• Hardly: In a severe or harsh manner. (कठिनाई से)
 
• Slowly: At a slow speed; not quickly. (धीरे से)
 
• Heavily: To a great degree; in large amounts. (भारी)
 
 
 
• "Heavily fined" means charging someone an amount of money as a punishment for not obeying a rule or law.
 
• So, as per the meaning of the given words "Heavily" should be used here.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: Drivers who violate this rule face hefty fines.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Complete sentence:* **Motorists committing this infraction are heavily __fined.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Latika said to him, "I got a hefty discount on this television."

options.text: Latika told him that she has got a hefty discount on that television.
Latika told him that she is getting a hefty discount on that television.
Latika told him that she had got a hefty discount on that television.
Latika told him that she has got a hefty discount on this television.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Latika told him that she had got a hefty discount on that television.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and we need to convert it to indirect speech.
 
• When we change a direct speech to an indirect speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" changes to "**told**" in the indirect speech.
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are replaced with the conjunction 'that' to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is removed in the indirect speech.
 
• The first word of the indirect speech should be in capital letters.
 
• The pronoun "**I**" changes with respect to the reporter i.e. "**she**" and the auxiliary verb changes as per the tense.
 
 
• The tense of the given direct speech is **simple past tense **which will be changed into** past perfect tense.**
 
• **Direct**: “I did the work”, he said.
 
• **Indirect**: He said that he had done the work.
 
 
 
 
 
• Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, indirect speech is - *Latika told him that she had got a hefty discount on that television.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

__Last before year__, Shirley got very good grades.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The year before last year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is: The year before last year**
 
• In this case, the phrase "the year before last year" is the most suitable choice because it accurately conveys the meaning that Shirley achieved good grades in the year prior to the year immediately preceding the current one.
 
• The rule that applies here is the use of ordinal numbers and the phrase "before last." In English, when referring to a year that is two years prior to the current one, it is common to use the phrase "the year before last year." This structure provides clarity and avoids ambiguity in the chronological sequence of events.
 
• Here's a breakdown of the components in the corrected sentence:
 
 
• "The year": This clarifies that we are referring to a specific time period, which is a year.
 
• "Before last year": This indicates that we are referring to the year preceding the one immediately before the current year.
 
• By using this phrase, we convey that Shirley got very good grades in the specific year prior to the year before the current one.
 
 

**Corrected sentence**: The year before last year, Shirley got very good grades.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The new owners hired a lot of new servers.

options.text: A lot of new servers were hired by the new owners.
A lot of new servers are being hired by the new owners.
A lot of new servers are hired by the new owners.
A lot of new servers had been hired by the new owners.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **A lot of new servers were hired by the new owners.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active form and we need to change it to the passive form.
 
• The given sentence is written in the simple past tense.
 
• The simple past tense in the active voice has the following structure: Subject + V2+ object__
 
• The simple past tense in the passive voice has the following structure: __Object+ was/were V3+ by + subject__
 
• Example - 
 
 
• Active voice - Rohan bought a pencil.
 
• Passive voice - A pencil was bought by Rohan..
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
 

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Passive Voice: *A lot of new servers were hired by the new owners.*

• **To **is used to indicate the person or thing that receives or experiences the object of the verb.

• So, the preposition "**to**" should be used here.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 2**, which contains an error in it.

 

**Corrected sentence:** *There is a whole world out there that is invisible to __the naked eye.*
